text: Does the opposite of what is needed. A massive distraction, just rewards you for doing nothing to the point where even if you're doing your Pomodoro properly (not aided by the fact this app doesn't have a break timer), your entire "break" gets used up doing busy work tending to your forest. text: If you really want a minimal app to help cut down screen time, please check out "Forest: Stay focused". This "Focus Plant" game is as much "for phone addiction" as Clash of Clans is. The only difference is the plant theme and a timer you set for resource generation. For an app that claims to help with phone addiction, there is an unfortunately time-consuming and extensive game to dive into right after each focus session. This game employs a lot of the casino/psychology gamification tactics that addicting games thrive off of. You're just trading apps to get addicted to. If you want an app that's basically setting a timer for when you'll be notified to play a game designed specifically to be time consuming, this app might be for you. The tiniest of 'progress' in the game requires tons of tapping, upgrading, resource generation, extensive game mechanics to get lost in, and within only a couple of focus sessions you're spreading your time and resources across many screens that require even more tapping, upgrading, resource generation, etc. I'd give it five stars if the game didn't pretend to be for phone addiction and just admitted it was a time-consuming game. As a game it's very cute and well designed, but claiming to be helpful for phone addiction while clearly being designed to be time consuming and addictive is a misleading way to describe it.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Hi, thank you for your feedback. Please share with us that which part of the game you think is too time consuming as we've been trying to keep the 'play time' minimal? The game is designed to psychological stimulate players, in other words, make the game addictive so that our players will keep coming back to focus as it's the only way to progress.

author: A Google user

text: While the app does what it's supposed to (encourage you to take breaks from your phone/tablet), the amount of time you have to spend "playing the game" is counterproductive. By "playing the game" I mean that in order to plant/grow/level up the plants, etc, I spent 30 minutes on the app ("playing") to do those tasks. These "tasks" (growing the garden) are a "reward" for not spending time on your phone. To spend 30 minutes on an app that is encouraging you to spend less time on your device seems counterintuitive to me. Also, the app sends notifications to tell you that you've got more 'rain' etc...(and the direction in the app suggests to keep notifications on and white list this app) which means the app is still encouraging you to have it within reach and respond to notifications; to then play a game. Makes more sense to delete the app and just put down my phone.
author: A Google user
developer_reply:
Hi, thank you for your feedback. Some planned updates to adjust your concerns:

1. Decrease play time: increase the water acceleration speed in the next update
2. Notification: we are considering to implement an on/off switch. The whale storage is 12 hours by default and increasing that might reduce the level of engagement.

text: I'm finding it increasingly difficult to complete a session. My session often ends after 3 minutes because my phone has locked and I have to watch an ad to get it back.
